title: 97 Maternal melatonin supplementation alters the transcriptomic profile of placenta in nutrient restricted cattle
content:
Abstract
The objective of this study is to investigate the effects of maternal nutrient restriction and dietary melatonin supplementation on the placental transcriptome. Maternal nutrition is a critical determinant of conceptus growth and development, with nutrient restriction leading to impaired fetal development and increased risk of metabolic diseases in later stages. Melatonin, known for its antioxidative properties and ability to cross the placenta, has emerged as a potential therapeutic agent to counteract the effects of nutrient restriction. In this study, 29 Brangus heifers (bred to a single sire via artificial insemination) on day 160 of gestation were assigned to a 2x2 factorial design. The animals were subjected to four treated groups: Adequately fed (ADQ-CON; 100% NRC Recommendation, n = 7), Nutrient Restricted (RES-CON; 60% NRC Recommendation, n = 7), and adequately fed or nutrient restricted supplemented with 20 mg/d of melatonin (ADQ-MEL, n = 7), and (RES-MEL, n = 8). Placental tissues were collected via cesarean section on day 240 of gestation and RNA-Seq analysis was conducted to analyze the transcriptome of placental tissue from 12 female and 17 male conceptuses. The samples were commercially analyzed by Zymo Research Corp, and the experimental data was further validated and visualized using R software version 4.4.2. We identified greater expression of UBOX5 in RES-MEL vs RES-CON group; and GRP in the RES-MEL vs ADQ-MEL group (Padj< 0.05). No significant differences in gene expression were observed between the nutrient restricted or control fed animals (RES vs ADQ). Two genes (ncRNA and CYP17A1) exhibited greater expression (Padj< 0.05) between melatonin versus control groups. Additionally, 13 differentially expressed genes (Padj< 0.05) were found in the conceptuses (Male vs Female); with nine gene upregulated in female conceptus and four gene upregulated in male conceptus. The upregulation of KDM6A (involved in Chromatin remodeling), CYP17A1 (Hormone synthesis regulator), UBA1 (involved in ubiquitin mediated pathways), and GREM1 (Protein tyrosine kinase regulation) in female conceptus compared to the male conceptus group, suggests enhanced metabolic activity, cellular differentiation, and conceptus growth. Considering the effect of conceptus gender and maternal melatonin treatment, we found greater expression of SFRP4 (modulates Wnt signaling pathway), ZNF82 (Transcription regulator), and ATP11C in the MEL-Male group compared to CON-Male group. These findings concludes that melatonin may modulate conceptus growth and development dependent on conceptus sex, with implications for better understanding the maternal and conceptus interactions.
